info.title: ERP platform API
info.description: Every action the screens perform. Sign in with POST /api/auth/sign-in (cookie, or set issueToken for a bearer token). Unsafe requests made with the cookie must send the header X-Erp-Request: 1. Each operation lists the permission it requires in x-erp-permission. Decimal values are JSON strings.

get.summary: Companies the caller may work in, a page at a time: word search on code and legal names, filters, sort, keyset or offset paging and grouping (the list query contract); by code by default.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text. Every word must occur (anywhere, any case) in at least one of the list's search fields; Arabic words also match the letter variants people type for one another (ا أ إ آ, ي ى, ه ة, و ؤ). Without a sort, rows come best match first (when at most 10,000 rows match; the page says ranked): words at the start of a field or of a word in it, the whole search equal to or starting a field, the words in the typed order; then shorter values, then the list's default sort.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter expression, for example: language eq 'ar' and (isActive eq true or lastSignInAt is null). Operators eq ne lt le gt ge contains startswith endswith in, is null, is not null; and, or, not, parentheses. Text in single quotes (double a quote inside), numbers with a dot, dates and times as ISO 8601 text.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sortable column keys separated by commas; a leading '-' sorts descending. Defaults to best match first when there is a search, else the list's default sort.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset paging: the 'next' value of the previous page. Cannot be combined with skip.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Offset paging: rows to skip. Cannot be combined with after.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 200 (default 50).

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: A groupable column key: the page also carries the groups of the filtered list with their counts and totals.

put.summary: Set the companies and branches one user may work in. Access is a grant: only companies and branches the caller works in can be given or taken away, only from users who hold no permission the caller lacks and work in no company or branch the caller does not; callers cannot change their own access. The request carries the version read; 409 when the access changed since.

get.summary: The caller's working company and branch, and the companies and branches they may switch to.

put.summary: Switch the caller's working company and branch (kept for their next sessions).

post.summary: Sign in with e-mail and password (or a one-time set-up code), or with a passkey (passkey, no e-mail or password: the device's answer to the challenge from GET /api/auth/session). Sets the session cookie; returns a bearer token too when issueToken is true. With newPassword it also changes the password; a set-up code answers 409 auth.passwordChangeRequired until one is given. After too many failed attempts at one address from one client, sign-in with that address from there answers 429 auth.signInPaused with pausedUntil and Retry-After, whether or not an account has the address, until the pause lifts or an administrator allows sign-in again. From a network address many clients share (a gateway or proxy), a browser that is not a known device of the account also gets sharedAddress true and a deviceCode (and the erp_pending cookie): once the user (POST /api/identity/me/devices/approve) or an administrator (POST /api/identity/users/{id}/devices/approve) enters that code, this browser signs in with its right password. Too many requests of any kind answer 429 request.tooMany.
post.x-erp-anonymous: Signing in is how a session starts.

post.summary: Revoke the current session and clear the cookie.
post.x-erp-anonymous: Signing out must work even when the session has already expired; it only ever revokes the caller's own session.

get.summary: The caller's session: user, workspace, permissions and menu, or authenticated = false with a fresh passkey sign-in challenge.

post.summary: Create a user with roles. Without a password the user is invited and the answer carries a one-time set-up code. Roles may only grant permissions the caller holds.

get.summary: One user.

put.summary: Change a user's name, language, active flag and roles. Only users whose access is within the caller's own; callers cannot change their own roles or deactivate themselves.

delete.summary: Delete a user who has never signed in (for example an invitation sent to a mistyped address). Anyone who has signed in keeps their record for the audit trail: deactivate them instead. Only a caller who holds every permission the user holds, never on themselves.

post.summary: Reset another user's password: a new one-time set-up code, or a given (temporary) password. Ends the user's sessions and, with removePasskeys, removes every passkey of theirs (a lost or stolen device). Only users whose access is within the caller's own.
Clear every sign-in pause on another user's account (failed attempts before now stop counting).

Sign another user out everywhere: ends all of their sessions and, with removePasskeys=true, removes every passkey of theirs, so no device signs back in without the password (a lost or stolen device). Only users whose access is within the caller's own.

get.summary: What the user can do and why: their roles, and every permission they hold with the roles that grant it.
The company the user works in by default (until they switch in the top bar), and the companies of the caller's they may work in.

put.summary: Set the company another user works in by default (null: their first company by code). Only a company of the caller's the user may work in, only for users whose access is within the caller's own and who work in no company the caller does not; never on oneself (switch in the top bar instead).

get.summary: The companies the caller works in: where the caller may assign roles that apply in one company, and name a default company.
The user's sign-in history, newest first (successes, failures, paused and refused attempts), and the clients paused now.

post.summary: Activate or deactivate every user the users list's search and filter match (the list's "all that match" selection). expectedCount must equal the number that match now, or nothing changes (409). The caller is never deactivated, and users holding a permission the caller lacks (workspace-wide or in one company) or any role in a company the caller does not work in are left alone; the answer counts each.

get.summary: Every permission in the catalogue with its label in the caller's language.

put.summary: Change the signed-in user's own preferences (interface language, digits on Arabic screens).

post.summary: Let one device of another user sign in while sign-in from its shared network address (a gateway or proxy) is paused: enter the device code its sign-in screen showed. For DeviceApprovalMinutes (60 by default) that browser, and no other, is a client of its own on this account: its right password signs in, and its first sign-in uses the approval up. A new approval replaces the last. Only users whose access is within the caller's own, never oneself (use POST /api/identity/me/devices/approve).

Let one of your own devices sign in while sign-in from its shared network address is paused: enter the device code its sign-in screen showed. Needs a session signed in within the last few minutes (403 auth.recentSignInRequiredDevice otherwise), so a browser left signed in cannot let other devices try the password.

get.summary: The signed-in user's passkeys, and until when this session may add one (a passkey is added only within a few minutes of signing in).

post.summary: Add a passkey: the browser's answer to the creation options. The answer must be for this site, made by a verified person, with an ES256 or RS256 key, and answer a challenge issued to this session.

Options for navigator.credentials.create(): a fresh challenge bound to this session, the user handle and the passkeys the device must not make again. 403 auth.recentSignInRequired when the session was signed in too long ago.

get.summary: One of the signed-in user's passkeys (name, dates and version, never its key).

delete.summary: Remove one of the signed-in user's passkeys: it no longer signs in (the device may still list it until the person deletes it there).

get.summary: Another user's passkeys (names and dates, never keys).

delete.summary: Remove another user's passkeys (a lost device, a person leaving): every one, or with passkeyId only that one (404 when the user holds no such passkey). Only for users whose access is within the caller's own, never on oneself.

delete.summary: Delete an exchange rate (amounts already converted keep the rate they were converted at). Idempotent: an id that names no rate of the workspace answers 204 as well, and nothing is written.

post.summary: Import exchange rates from a CSV file's text (columns currency, date, rate, and optionally quote_currency and reference; at most 20,000 lines). Nothing is saved unless every line is valid.

get.summary: The audit log: every recorded change of the business records the caller may read (each kind of record needs its own read permission as well, in the record's company), newest first, a page at a time: word search on the record's name, filters (actorId, actorKind, action, recordType, record, recordId, fields eq 'email', occurredAt), sort, keyset or offset paging and grouping (the list query contract).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text. Every word must occur (anywhere, any case) in at least one of the list's search fields; Arabic words also match the letter variants people type for one another (ا أ إ آ, ي ى, ه ة, و ؤ). Without a sort, rows come best match first (when at most 10,000 rows match; the page says ranked): words at the start of a field or of a word in it, the whole search equal to or starting a field, the words in the typed order; then shorter values, then the list's default sort.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter expression, for example: language eq 'ar' and (isActive eq true or lastSignInAt is null). Operators eq ne lt le gt ge contains startswith endswith in, is null, is not null; and, or, not, parentheses. Text in single quotes (double a quote inside), numbers with a dot, dates and times as ISO 8601 text.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sortable column keys separated by commas; a leading '-' sorts descending. Defaults to best match first when there is a search, else the list's default sort.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset paging: the 'next' value of the previous page. Cannot be combined with skip.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Offset paging: rows to skip. Cannot be combined with after.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 200 (default 50).

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: A groupable column key: the page also carries the groups of the filtered list with their counts and totals.

get.summary: One change of the audit log with every field's old and new value as stored, and the names of the records its values refer to by id (where the caller may read them). A change the caller may not read does not exist for them (404).

The history of one record, newest change first: who changed it, when, and each field's old and new value (a creation lists every first value, a deletion every last value). Besides the audit log's permission, the caller needs the permission that reads such records, in the record's company (and its branch, where they may work in only some): otherwise, as for an id that names nothing, the history is empty. With type (schema.table, as /api/lists/audit.log/definition names the kinds of records), only that kind's changes, and for rows a form shows by another record's id (a user's company access by the user's id) every row whose owner column held the id.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The kind of record (schema.table, for example identity.users); without it every change of the record, whatever its kind.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The id of the last change shown: older changes follow it.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Changes per page, 1 to 200 (default 50).

Money.description:
An amount of money as the ledger rule requires it: the amount in its currency, the exchange
    rate used, and the amount in the base currency, together with which currency that base is
    (companies of one tenant may keep different base currencies). Decimal only — never floating
    point.
    Rounding follows the owner-signed rule docs/compliance/vat-rounding-and-currency.md. Rule 1:
a figure rounds to its currency's minor units half away from zero. Rule 2: rounding happens
once, on the figure that is stated; lines and subtotals keep their full precision. So a
Money is either unrounded (a line or a subtotal: the default) or
stated (Money Money.State() rounded it once). An unrounded money carries the exact
amount, and its exact base amount is always Amount × ExchangeRate; Money Money.Add(Money other)
sums the exact figures and never the rounded base amounts, so three lines of USD 1.00 at
3.6725 total AED 11.0175, stated as 11.02 (not 3.67 + 3.67 + 3.67 = 11.01). Stated figures
add as stated figures (a statement of two invoices sums what each invoice stated). Mixing the
two would round part of a total twice, so Money Money.Add(Money other) refuses it.
    Stored as `numeric(28,10)` amount, `numeric(19,8)` rate, `numeric(19,4)` base
    amount, `char(3)` currencies and a `boolean` stated flag (MoneyMapping).
    Every figure goes through Money Money.Create(decimal amount, CurrencyCode currency, decimal exchangeRate, CurrencyCode baseCurrency), Money Money.Unrounded(decimal amount, CurrencyCode currency, decimal exchangeRate, CurrencyCode baseCurrency) or Money Money.InBase(decimal amount, CurrencyCode currency),
and the operations on them: the properties have no setters (no object initialiser and no
with expression can set a base amount that disagrees with the amount and the rate), JSON
is read through MoneyJsonConverter (which builds with Money Money.Unrounded(decimal amount, CurrencyCode currency, decimal exchangeRate, CurrencyCode baseCurrency)), and
the database reads the columns back through the constructor. The one figure no factory makes is
default(Money), which has no currency: every operation refuses it.
